description: Somos Kuntur Labs, un equipo con muchas ganas de participar en el NASA Space Apps Challenge y crear una solución innovadora usando datos y tecnología espacial. Nos interesa la exploración del espacio, la tecnología y aprender trabajando en equipo.
summary: Alto Intiorko in Tacna, Peru, covers an analysis area equivalent to about 44 football pitches. WasteWard helps a municipality decide which sectors to check first and translate confirmed exposed areas into cover-soil and truck-trip scenarios. We combine dated NASA/USGS Landsat optical and thermal observations with the official OEFA boundary, dividing the pilot into 111 sectors. An experimental priority index combines optical signal, persistence and thermal contrast; the published dataset contains 22 dates and 2,442 sector observations. Time-series views support exploratory Mann-Kendall and Sen slope analysis. We also compared Landsat and Sentinel-2 optical signals and checked historical fires against NASA FIRMS. The dashboard makes dates, data quality, assumptions and limitations visible. It does not claim calibrated waste detection, fire prediction or measured methane by sector. Our next step is independent field validation with the municipality to test whether the ranking improves inspection and cover planning.
details:
PROBLEM AND INTENDED USER

Alto Intiorko is a municipal waste site in Ciudad Nueva, Tacna, Peru. The pilot addresses a decision for the Municipalidad Provincial de Tacna: which sectors should be checked first, and how much cover material might be needed once the exposed area is established? Our analysis polygon is approximately 317,507 m2, equivalent to about 44 football pitches of 105 x 68 m. This is an area comparison, not daily waste volume or verified exposed waste.

HOW IT WORKS AND CHALLENGE ALIGNMENT

WasteWard combines NASA/USGS Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance and surface temperature with the OEFA boundary. The published snapshot contains 111 clipped analysis sectors, 22 acquisition dates and 2,442 sector-date observations. Users inspect optical and thermal variables across dates, see where the priority changes, and consult exploratory Mann-Kendall and Sen slope thermal analysis. The latest usable evaluation in this snapshot is 15 October 2026. The 31 October acquisition is incorporated but fails the filters for a complete evaluation. A snapshot is not a real-time satellite feed.

Our proposed IPP weights optical signal at 55%, persistence at 25% and thermal contrast at 20%. These are team-defined operational weights, not a published or independently calibrated standard. Persistence uses compatible valid observations in a 120-day window. Missing components remain explicit. The 60 m analysis grid does not increase the native thermal resolution. Methane scenarios are separate from the IPP and do not locate emissions by sector.

The municipal workflow ranks sectors, supports selecting them for review, records a confirmed or explicitly assumed exposed fraction, then calculates placed soil as exposed area multiplied by scenario thickness. A detailed planner adds editable loose-material and truck-capacity assumptions. The ten high-priority sectors total about 35,998 m2. Assuming 100% of that area needs 0.25 m of cover gives about 8,999 m3; assuming 50% gives about 4,500 m3. Neither is measured demand or an engineering prescription.

EVIDENCE AND LIMITATIONS

A comparison of valid optical signals in 111 sectors uses Landsat on 15 October and Sentinel-2 on 12 October 2026: Spearman correlation 0.826, seven shared sectors in the optical top ten, and two in the top five. This is cross-sensor consistency, not detection accuracy or full-IPP validation. Both sensors can confuse bare soil with waste. There are currently no independent current sector labels for exposed-waste accuracy.

A retrospective check of complete 2025 Peru NASA FIRMS archives found five nearby VIIRS detections in November: four early on 20 November in Tacna and one on 28 November. All pixel centers lie outside the OEFA boundary, about 14-240 m away. These provide temporal context near documented fires, not confirmed burned sectors or predictive validation. The preceding published Landsat scene on 21 November had a maximum thermal contrast of only +0.50 C and no complete IPP. We do not claim that the system anticipated the fire. Regional NASA POWER weather was also explored as context, not local gust measurements or causal proof.

DIFFERENTIATION AND INTENDED IMPACT

The contribution connects dated Earth-observation evidence to an explainable sector shortlist and a transparent resource scenario in one dashboard. For the municipality, the intended value is a clearer basis for inspections and cover planning. For OEFA and residents, the intended value is traceable information about evidence, dates and assumptions. Municipal adoption, time savings, prevention benefits and actual cover outcomes have not been measured. No institutional partnership or endorsement is claimed. The next step is blinded validation using independent, dated, geolocated observations, including bare-soil controls and separate evaluation data.

IMPLEMENTATION AND AI DISCLOSURE

We used Python for geospatial processing and JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Leaflet for the public dashboard hosted on Vercel. Satellite observations are sourced data, not AI-generated measurements. AI assistance supported coding, analysis, writing and conceptual presentation illustrations. The 30-second video was composed with Remotion and FFmpeg. Its narration is a real recording by a team member, edited for timing and loudness; it is not a cloned or AI-generated voice. Generated images carry a visible AI watermark; they are not photographs, measured maps or evidence of current site conditions. No trained waste-detection model is claimed. An exploratory methane model and NASA EMIT/AIRS investigations are supplementary and do not provide methane measurements by 60 m sector.
